task.description:
WF-03 Step 2b -- HARD GATE on CODE-DESIGNER's fix design for ISS-0109. The design artefact is lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md. You are the only check on it before implementation begins; there is no human reviewer (core-directives.md, Humanless Operation). A validator that reads the producer's result.summary and agrees has validated nothing -- RE-DERIVE every verdict below from the code and the documents themselves.

Read: lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md in full, then handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-02-code-designer.json, then handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json (the diagnosis the design is built on).

Your standard checks apply (covers every acceptance criterion, contains no implementation code, unambiguous enough to build from). Beyond those, this design makes SIX specific claims that are load-bearing and individually checkable. Check each one AT THE SOURCE, and state per claim: CONFIRMED or REFUTED, with the evidence you used.

CLAIM 1 -- "Not a production defect." The design refutes the Step 1 lead that insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -> re_select_registration/1 can return {:ok, registration} for a schema that does not exist, on the grounds that provision_tenant_schema/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:164) runs CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS UNCONDITIONALLY at :188 inside the same transaction, BEFORE reaching insert_or_fetch_registration/2 at :190, so the pre-existing-row branch at :483-:488 can never return naming an absent schema. Read those lines yourself. Verify specifically: (i) that :188 is genuinely unconditional and not inside a branch skipped on the pre-existing path; (ii) that :188 and :190 are inside ONE transaction opened at :170; (iii) that no other caller reaches the registration path without going through :188. If any of the three fails, the design's central structural claim fails and this is a FAIL.

CLAIM 2 -- "Completeness is a decided invariant, not a defect." The design declines to guarantee table completeness inside provision_tenant_schema/1 because lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:288-294's "No implicit chaining invariant" decides it, and core-directives.md forbids silently re-deciding a decided record. Read req022's lines 288-294 yourself and confirm they actually say what the design says they say. This is the highest-risk claim in the design: if it is a misreading, the design has declined a real production fix on a false authority. If the record genuinely decides it, the design is RIGHT to decline and you must say so.

CLAIM 3 -- "C1 fails first, deterministically." The design's headline regression case drops the promotion_assertion_runs table while leaving the schema AND schema_migrations intact, and asserts that PRE-FIX the fixture still passes -- because Ecto's Migrator sees the version already recorded and re-applies nothing, so replay_migrations/1 returns {:ok, _} against an incomplete schema. This is the claim that makes the whole regression suite meaningful; if replay actually recreates the table, C1 passes pre-fix and proves nothing. Settle it: read the replay path (tenant_provisioning.ex:238-264) and Migrator's semantics, and if you can settle it by RUNNING something cheap against the test database rather than by reasoning, do that -- constructing the state and observing replay's return value is worth far more than an argument about it.

CLAIM 4 -- "The 19-table oracle is legal because of a both-directions rot guard." A hard-coded table list is exactly the kind of duplicated constant that goes stale silently. Verify: (i) the count and names actually match what the tenant migration manifest produces today -- derive the real list yourself rather than trusting the design's; (ii) the specified guard test genuinely fails in BOTH directions (a table added to the manifest but not the oracle, AND a table removed from the manifest but left in the oracle). A one-direction guard is a FAIL on this item.

CLAIM 5 -- "C2 is a characterization test, not the regression." The design flags that C2 (drop the schema, leave the registry row) proves FIXTURE detection rather than any production behaviour change. Confirm the design does not anywhere present C2 as evidence of a production fix, and that the distinction is stated where TEST-DESIGNER will actually see it.

CLAIM 6 -- SCOPE DISCIPLINE. Confirm the design proposes no fix for ISS-0110/GH#364 (reaper min_age), ISS-0111/GH#365 (identity_migration_test bulk delete), ISS-0112/GH#366 (the other 39 copy-paste sites), ISS-0113/GH#367 (Sandbox.mode(:auto) leak) or ISS-0107/GH#357 (nested mix test), AND that no part of its rationale DEPENDS on any of them being fixed. Also confirm helper adoption is limited to the two modules ISS-0109 names.

ALSO CHECK, and this one is about honesty rather than correctness: the design's FIXED-vs-INSTRUMENTED verdict says INSTRUMENTED, not FIXED, and recommends NOT closing ISS-0109. Confirm that verdict is consistent with what the design actually delivers -- i.e. that the design does not elsewhere claim or imply a root cause has been removed. ORCH sets ISS-0109's final status from this verdict, so an overstated one would put a false 'resolved' into a registry six other issues cross-reference. If you believe the verdict is WRONG IN EITHER DIRECTION -- overstated, or understated because the design does remove a real root cause -- say so.

VERDICT RULES: PASS only if every acceptance criterion is met AND all six claims are CONFIRMED. FAIL if any claim is REFUTED, naming the specific gap per acceptance criterion (not a general impression) so CODE-DESIGNER's rework is narrowly scoped. A design that is merely thinner than you would have written it is not a FAIL; a design resting on a misread source is.

CONSTRAINTS: do not edit the design yourself -- you gate it, CODE-DESIGNER reworks it. Toolchain here is Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against a 1.18.3-otp-27 pin (ISS-0106, filed, not yours), so `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` fail on main for unrelated reasons; use plain `mix compile`/`mix test`. Postgres for this workspace is on LETFLOW_DB_PORT from ./.env. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename, never `git add -A`.


================================================================================
RE-GATE after CODE-DESIGNER rework iteration 1 (commit bf87afb) -- dispatched by
ORCH 2026-08-21T01:55:45Z. This is a NARROW re-gate, not a fresh full review.
================================================================================

You FAILed this design on one defect in SS3.2 plus two MINOR wording items in SS2.2 and
one ambiguity in SS3.5. CODE-DESIGNER reports all four addressed. Your own prior verdict
already CONFIRMED all six load-bearing claims and passed sections 2, 5, 7 and 8 -- do NOT
re-review those. Re-derive only the following, and only from source:

1. SS3.2's corrected opts contract. CODE-DESIGNER reports opts now carries NO :status key
   at all, and that Tenant.create_changeset/3 is called with exactly two cast attributes
   (slug, display_name) plus opts[:oidc_mode] as the THIRD POSITIONAL argument, defaulting
   to :disabled. Verify against lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex (the enum at :56 and the
   create_changeset/3 head/spec around :76-79) and against both fixture call sites. The
   specific thing to check: that the corrected contract now PRESERVES today's behaviour --
   both adopted sites currently land on the schema default :active because neither sets a
   status, and the corrected helper must do the same. A contract that merely swaps one
   illegal value for a legal one but still SETS a status would not satisfy INV-F-5.

2. SS3.5's capture_schema_state/1 failure boundary. CODE-DESIGNER reports it is now nested
   rather than competing: a single failing query is ALWAYS a per-field degradation
   returning {:ok, schema_state()}, and {:error, {:capture_failed, _}} is an outer net for
   failures outside the per-field guards. Check one specific consequence they claim to have
   closed, because it is the one that could produce a MISLEADING report: if tables_present
   degrades to [], tables_missing must also be [] -- NOT "all 19 missing" -- since an
   unobserved set must never be reported as an observed absence. Confirm the artefact
   actually says this, normatively, and that the same rule is stated for
   applied_versions/versions_missing.

3. SS2.2's two narrowings: that req022:288-294 is now quoted verbatim and its scope limited
   to what it actually decides (that provision_tenant_schema/1 never CALLS
   replay_migrations/2), with the narrower variants declined on their own merits rather
   than on the record's authority; and that req022 is now cited as a gate-approved design
   artefact under lib/letflow/design/ rather than as a docs/migration/decisions/ record.
   Confirm the OUTCOME is unchanged -- production code still untouched, so this run stays
   test-only and SECURITY-REVIEWER's tenant-data-path trigger stays unarmed. If the
   narrowing has quietly opened a door to a production change, that is a FAIL.

4. DIFF CONFINEMENT. CODE-DESIGNER claims the diff touches only SS2.2, SS3.2 and SS3.5, and
   that sections 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 are untouched. Verify with
   `git diff a8ced05 bf87afb -- lib/letflow/design/iss0109-*.md` rather than taking the
   claim. A rework that silently edited a section this gate already passed is itself a
   finding, regardless of whether the edit is an improvement.

5. Still no implementation code (function bodies) anywhere in the artefact.

VERDICT: PASS if items 1-5 all hold. FAIL only on a genuine remaining defect in these five
-- do not fail it for something you did not raise in the first pass and that is not a new
regression introduced by the rework. If you find something in a previously-passed section
that you now believe is wrong, do NOT silently fold it into this verdict: report it as a
separate MINOR issue in result.issues so ORCH can decide whether it warrants its own
rework, and say plainly that you missed it on the first pass.
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of step-02-code-designer.json is checked against the design artefact itself and a per-criterion met/not-met verdict is given
The design contains no implementation code (function bodies) -- verified by reading, not assumed

CLAIM 1 (CREATE SCHEMA at tenant_provisioning.ex:188 is unconditional, inside the transaction opened at :170, and unavoidable on the pre-existing-registration path) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED against the actual source lines
CLAIM 2 (req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:288-294 genuinely decides the no-implicit-chaining invariant) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED by reading that record directly

CLAIM 3 (C1 fails first: replay_migrations/1 returns {:ok, _} against a schema with a dropped table whose version is still recorded) is settled -- preferably by constructing the state and observing replay's actual return value rather than by argument alone
CLAIM 4 (the hard-coded table oracle matches the manifest today, and its rot guard fails in BOTH directions) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED, with the real table list derived independently
CLAIM 5 (C2 is presented as a characterization test, not as evidence of a production fix) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED
CLAIM 6 (no fix designed for ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113/0107, no rationale depending on them, helper adoption limited to the two named modules) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED
An explicit judgement is given on whether the INSTRUMENTED-not-FIXED verdict is consistent with what the design delivers, including whether it is understated
A single overall verdict (PASS or FAIL) is stated, and on FAIL each gap is named per acceptance criterion so rework is narrowly scoped

result.summary:
RE-GATE VERDICT (rework iteration 1, commit bf87afb): PASS. All five re-gate items re-derived from source; sections 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and the six load-bearing claims were not re-reviewed (already closed by the first pass).

ITEM 1 -- SS3.2's corrected opts contract: PASS, and it genuinely PRESERVES today's behaviour. lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:56 is field(:status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:active, :migrating], default: :active); create_changeset/3's @spec and head at :76-79 are create_changeset(tenant, attrs, oidc_mode) when oidc_mode in [:enabled, :disabled] -- the third argument is the OIDC mode, not a status. The reworked artefact's @type opts (design line ~195) now reads oidc_mode: :enabled | :disabled and carries NO :status key at all; SS3.2 step 2 specifies exactly two cast attributes (slug:, display_name:) plus opts[:oidc_mode] as the third positional argument defaulting to :disabled, and line 258 states explicitly 'Consequently opts carries no :status key. Omitting the field is what preserves today's behaviour: both adopted sites currently get the schema default :active.' That is behaviour preservation, not merely a legal-value swap: I re-read both call sites -- promotion_test.exs:62-72 and promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs:95-105 pass %{slug:, display_name:} only, with :disabled as the third positional arg -- so neither sets a status today and the corrected helper sets none either. The future-extension note (a later adopter may add :status constrained to :active | :migrating, MUST NOT be added speculatively here) does not set a status now. The MAJOR from the first pass is closed.

ITEM 2 -- SS3.5's capture_schema_state/1 failure boundary: PASS. The two rules are now explicitly nested and marked normative. Design lines 362-376 state: each field is gathered inside its own guard and 'A single failing query is always a per-field degradation, never a whole-call failure', returning {:ok, schema_state()}; and the specific consequence ORCH asked about IS stated normatively at lines 368-371: 'If tables_present degraded to [], then tables_missing is [] as well -- not "all 19 missing" -- because an unobserved set must never be reported as an observed absence. Same for applied_versions/versions_missing.' The same rule is therefore stated for the versions pair, as required. {:error, {:capture_failed, exception}} is now scoped as 'the outer safety net only... not reachable by any single field's query failing.' The first pass's MINOR ambiguity is closed.

ITEM 3 -- SS2.2's two narrowings, outcome unchanged: PASS. req022:288-294 is now quoted verbatim inside SS2.2 and its scope limited to what it decides (provision_tenant_schema/1 never CALLS replay_migrations/2 and vice versa). The narrower variants (verify tables / return a new error) are explicitly declared 'not literally decided by req022' and declined on their own merits -- that verifying completeness inside the provisioning primitive would make it assert an outcome it is not the step responsible for producing, and would give it a failure mode no caller in lib/ can currently cause. req022 is now correctly cited as a gate-approved design artefact under lib/letflow/design/, with the note that core-directives.md's unoverridable docs/migration/decisions/ clause does not itself bind, and that the correct route would be REVIEWER sign-off -- not needed because the design DECLINES the contradiction. No door to a production change was opened: SS2.3 still reads 'No production change. lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex are not modified by this design' and 'SECURITY-REVIEWER's tenant-data-path trigger is therefore not armed'; INV-F-2 (SS4, untouched) restates it; SS9's prohibitions are untouched. Run stays test-only.

ITEM 4 -- DIFF CONFINEMENT: PASS, verified with `git diff a8ced05 bf87afb -- lib/letflow/design/iss0109-*.md` rather than from the claim. Five hunks, +102/-30 lines, at new-file lines ~118-146, ~193, ~232-262, ~271-278 and ~352-381. Mapped against the artefact's own heading offsets (SS2.2 = 110-150, SS3.2 = 181-284, SS3.5 = 334-384), every hunk lands inside SS2.2, SS3.2 or SS3.5. Sections 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 are byte-identical between a8ced05 and bf87afb. No silent edit to a previously-passed section. (The same commit also touches step-02-code-designer.json and this handoff file; that is bookkeeping, outside the artefact.)

ITEM 5 -- NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE: PASS, verified by reading. The artefact still has exactly two fenced blocks: lines 186-227 (@type tenant_fixture, @type opts, @spec provisioned_tenant!/1, @type schema_state, @spec capture_schema_state/1, @spec assert_schema_complete!/2, @spec expected_tenant_tables/0 -- declarations only) and lines 293-298 (a bare comma-separated list of the 19 table names). No def/defp, no function bodies, no .ex/.exs source anywhere.

OVERALL: PASS. The design is now buildable as written; ELIXIR-DEV following SS3.2 literally produces a helper whose tenant rows keep today's default status :active. Two MINOR notes below are recorded for the record and are NOT rework blockers.

issues.description: Introduced by the rework (and mirrored in ORCH's own re-gate wording): SS3.2 line 258-259 cites '(INV-F-5)' as the invariant that landing on the schema default :active preserves. INV-F-5 (SS4) is about TEARDOWN behaviour being today's three statements unchanged; there is no invariant in SS4 covering the tenant row's status field. The substance of SS3.2 is correct -- no status is set -- only the cross-reference label is wrong. Cosmetic; does not warrant a rework cycle on its own, but should be corrected if SS3.2 is edited again.

MISSED ON MY FIRST PASS -- reported separately rather than folded into this verdict, as instructed. INV-F-4 in SS4 (a section this gate already passed, untouched by the rework) states capture_schema_state/1's never-raises contract as 'it returns {:error, {:capture_failed, _}}', which reads as though that tuple is the general failure return. The reworked SS3.5 now sharpens the boundary so that a single failing query returns {:ok, degraded_state} and {:error, {:capture_failed, _}} is only the outer net. INV-F-4 is not contradicted (it asserts non-raising, which still holds) but its wording is now looser than SS3.5's normative rule and could mislead an implementer who reads the invariant table alone. ORCH's call whether this warrants its own one-line rework.

result.next_action: Design PASSES the hard gate. Advance WF-03 to the implementation step (ELIXIR-DEV / TEST-DESIGNER per the workflow) against lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md at commit bf87afb. No further CODE-DESIGNER rework is required. The two MINOR items are documentation-accuracy notes ORCH may fold into a later edit or ignore; neither blocks implementation. ISS-0109's status should still be set from SS8.3 (INSTRUMENTED, not FIXED -- do not close), unchanged from the first pass.
